name: MI-05
label: Safe R

key_factors: Strong Republican district with a +13 Republican partisan lean
Incumbent Tim Walberg running with a large financial advantage
Democratic challenger raised only about $56,000 with no outside support
Prediction markets price the Republican near 92%
model.rationale: The district's Republican lean, Walberg's incumbency, and his roughly 30-to-1 fundraising edge over Christian Vukasovich leave the Democrat with no visible path, and markets agree at about a 7% Democratic win probability. The forecast stays near the fundamentals-based margin of roughly minus 16.
model.watch: A major late Democratic outside-spending intervention or a polling surprise showing the race within single digits would warrant a relook.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Republican Tim Walberg seeks another term in a southern Michigan district that leans about 13 points Republican at the presidential level. He is a well-established incumbent with nearly $1 million on hand, while Democrat Christian Vukasovich has raised under $60,000 and shows no outside spending on either side. Minor-party and independent candidates are on the ballot but lack resources.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, money, and prediction markets, all of which point the same way. Walberg is a heavy favorite, with the main uncertainty being turnout patterns in a low-information contest.
